questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was not too far away from Denmark, but still far away enough to experience a different culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got sick while I was there something with my eyes that made the whole experience a little harder because I was back and forth for 4 months in the italian health system that is very speciel I must say - therefor an 8 but if it had not been for that for sure a 10 - I really loved the city and the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A little hard also because their system is very different from Copenhagens system. But I just wrote a lot with the unimi, and that helped a lot - so just keep un writing till u feel secure what is going to happen when you arrive.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got emails - but you need to know that it is on your new email connected to your new university u will get very little information when you arrive on your alumni email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were no intro week which I found very sad, so we did not get to meet new people at the beginning and get an introduction on how to do the things you needed that came very late and only because we asked the other italian students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We were three people trying to find a home and it ws very hard, we first had an airbnb, but that was not room for us all so we forund the apartment through idealist - but it was a little sketchy and would only recommend if you already are in the city and can come look at it in person.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very pricy and hard to find. Also I think you will get a lot more friends from other countries if you live on campus!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very hard and I think I registered course in the last month I was there, they do it very different than in Copenhagen, but on the other hand you can just surf around classes and see what suits you, so very unstressful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was through unimi and you just had to write your class, teacher and acts points in a scheme and that was it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could always ask your teacher, other student or write to the unimi mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful I got all the classes I wanted, I do not think they have a limit.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything will work out do not stress about it because the Italians don't. Forget about the strict and stressed process in Copenhagen and just try all the classes you think sounds interesting and after that you just choose the once that fits the ects points and then all will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very special and very easy standards also very little cases were in English so most of the classes you can pick is philosophy if you study at the humanistic faculty.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is very low, I only took MA classes and the level was way lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, like I said the level is much lower and the teachers do not care for it as much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biopolitics
Philosophy of mind
Workshop: iconography and iconology
Intellectuals, popular culture, collective identities: Italy and Europe in the 19th and 20th centuries

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend biopolitics because it was interesting but also because Andrea the teacher was a lot of fun. 
And if you wanna learn about the italian history do take the last cause listed.

questions.answer: No idea.

questions.answer: still no idea.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to verona, lake como, and Genova (repella)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go talk with them they love it and are so sweet and helpful. Also they have Erasmus bars you can meet people on.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, because there is a lot of people who cannot speak English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the food, the drinks and the going out culture just for an aperol or pasta.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, eat out a lot, go swimming in the weekends and take a food course.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The leves is very low and the exams are very weird, so do not stress to much just be prepared and know that you can wait for 7 ours before it is your turn to have your exam - also the oral exams will be in front of your class mates - you are never alone with a teacher.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another city and being with my new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The italian health system beaucse I got sick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You will love it - and look for places like Nolo or Navigli <3

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
